title: Unit – 4 : Session – 2 | Innateness, Inheritance and Human Participation
sections: Q1. INHERITANCE of each order: the MATERIAL order inherits constitution — an atom of gold remains gold, generation after generation of a material unit retains its composition. The PRANIC order inherits the SEED — a mango seed grows into a mango tree, not a neem tree; the species' method is inherited through the seed. The ANIMAL order inherits the BREED — the offspring of a cow is a cow, with the bodily characteristics and instincts of the breed. The HUMAN order inherits education-SANSKAR — a human child is born with a body like the parents, but its understanding, values and conduct are decided by what education and sanskar it receives, not by birth. This is why human conduct is not fixed by lineage.

Q2. EDUCATION-SANSKAR alone decides whether a human being lives with human conduct or inhuman conduct. HUMAN sanskar = commitment, preparation and practice of living with right understanding and right feeling — it produces definite, harmonious conduct (trust, respect, right utilisation). INHUMAN sanskar = conditioning toward 'physical facility is everything' — it produces indefinite conduct: exploitation, competition, unlimited consumption. Two children of the same parents can turn out opposite because sanskar differs; hence the problem and the solution of all human conflict lie in education-sanskar, not in biology.

Q3. HUMAN PARTICIPATION for mutual fulfilment: (a) toward the MATERIAL order — right utilisation (use only as per need, never waste) and participation in its cyclical processes; (b) toward the PRANIC order — PRESERVATION and enrichment: protecting soil, forests, seeds, promoting biodiversity; (c) toward the ANIMAL order — PROTECTION: freedom from cruelty, preservation of habitats and species; (d) toward the HUMAN order — ensuring right understanding and right feeling (PROSPERITY thinking and relationship) in every human being. When humans participate thus, all four orders are mutually fulfilled — this participation itself is the human value in existence.

Q4. Reflection: in my own family I can see sanskar at work — habits of saving, sharing or quarrelling were absorbed at home long before any formal education. Recognising that conduct is decided by education-sanskar and not by 'genes' or 'fate' is empowering: whatever unhelpful sanskar I have inherited can be re-examined and replaced through self-exploration, and whatever I pass on to younger siblings is my responsibility. Inheritance in humans is thus a matter of choice and education, not destiny.
